newsitem.title: CANADA: Poll shows support for Quebec sovereignty tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows support for Quebec sovereignty tumbles.

text.p: A CROP poll for the Canadian Broadcasting Corp and La Presse found that voter support for Quebec sovereignty has tumbled, the French-language daily newspaper said on Wednesday.

The survey showed 35 percent of Quebec voters polled were in favor of a sovereign Quebec, with or without an association with Canada. In March 1996, Quebec voter support for sovereignty under those terms was at 45 percent.
"Sovereignty loses some feathers," said the La Presse headline on the poll.
The survey also showed that 42 percent of Quebec voters prefer that the province remain in Canada, but get more powers, while 21 percent prefer the status quo.
In the poll, 51 percent of Canadians said they think it is possible or very possible that Quebec will separate by the year 2000. Among Quebec respondents, 56 percent agreed.
The poll of 2,541 Canadians April 17 to 22 had a margin of error of two percent, 19 times out of 20, La Presse said.
